title: Exponential-Time Decision of Bounded Acceptance
statement: Let $\mathrm{EXPCOM}$ be the language of Boolean words $z$ for which there are Boolean words $\alpha,x$ and a natural number $n$ such that $z=\langle\alpha,\langle x,1^n\rangle\rangle$ and the machine decoded from $\alpha$ accepts $x$ within $2^n$ steps. There exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $D$ and natural numbers $A,B$ such that, for every input of length $m$, $D$ decides membership in $\mathrm{EXPCOM}$ within $A\,2^{B(m+1)}$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: The language $\mathrm{EXPCOM}$ is defined by the stated encoded bounded-acceptance condition

For every input length $m$, $D$ decides $\mathrm{EXPCOM}$ within $A2^{B(m+1)}$ steps
